newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada board sets hearing for gas liquids project.
newsitem.headline: Canada board sets hearing for gas liquids project.

text.p: Canada's National Energy Board said on Friday it would hold a public hearing on Amoco Corp unit Amoco Canada Petroleum Co Ltd's plans to expand its natural gas liquids pipeline in southwestern Saskatchewan.

Amoco applied to build a 155 km (96 mile) gas liquids pipeline to IPL Energy Inc unit Interprovincial Pipe Line's transmission line at Kerrobert, Saskatchewan from NGL extraction plants at Empress, Alberta.
The Kerrobert pipeline moves all the gas liquids from the Amoco, Empress Gas Liquids Joint Venture and PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd extraction plants plus some volumes produced at a Petro-Canada plant.
The C$23 million expansion would twin the existing pipeline to meet increases in NGL production from Empress, the NEB said.
The new line would boost gas liquids throughput capability by about 50,000 barrels a day to 117,000 barrels a day starting in November 1997, the NEB said.
The board said the hearing would start in Calgary on June 16 and interventions were to be filed by May 14.
